Hypothesis: We hypothesize that bioengineered, tumor-specific exosomes that are co-loaded with miR-128-3p and integrated with a near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent tracking system can restore oxaliplatin sensitivity in resistant colorectal cancer. Specifically, the exosomes—engineered with precise tumor-targeting ligands—will selectively deliver miR-128-3p to chemoresistant cancer cells, where the miRNA will downregulate Bmi1. This downregulation is expected to reduce MRP5-mediated drug efflux and modulate other EMT-related signaling pathways, thereby reversing EMT as evidenced by the restoration of epithelial markers. The built-in NIR tracking module enables real-time monitoring of exosome biodistribution and payload release, providing immediate feedback for dynamic therapeutic adjustments. This multi-layered strategy leverages contemporary nanotechnology and imaging capabilities to address the mechanistic steps of drug resistance and EMT, thereby offering a robust and clinically translatable intervention.
Abstract: This study proposes a novel therapeutic strategy to overcome oxaliplatin resistance in colorectal cancer by employing bioengineered, tumor-specific exosomes co-loaded with miR-128-3p and integrated with a near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent tracking module. The exosomes are surface-modified with select tumor-targeting ligands to ensure preferential uptake by chemoresistant cells. Once internalized, miR-128-3p is released to downregulate Bmi1, a key regulator of drug resistance, leading to decreased MRP5-mediated drug efflux and modulation of additional epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-related pathways. This cascade results in EMT reversal—restoring epithelial markers—and ultimately, enhanced chemosensitivity to oxaliplatin. The integrated NIR tracking system not only allows real-time monitoring of exosome biodistribution and payload release but also facilitates dynamic treatment adjustments, mitigating off-target effects and addressing compensatory tumor signaling. This refined approach builds on established components while incorporating advanced imaging and targeted delivery innovations to ensure practical implementability and improved clinical outcomes.
CausalChain: Exosome engineering with tumor-targeting ligands and NIR tracking -> Synthetic enrichment of miR-128-3p in exosomes -> Specific uptake by oxaliplatin-resistant colorectal cancer cells -> miR-128-3p downregulates Bmi1 -> Bmi1 reduction leads to decreased MRP5 expression and modulation of EMT-related pathways -> Reversal of EMT (restoration of epithelial markers) -> Enhanced chemosensitivity to oxaliplatin
